channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
item.description: The method replaces per-prediction trust in foundation-model perturbation response outputs with a calibrated confidence score, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, motivated by the finding that the ST decoder's first attention layer is low-rank (projecting onto 4-32 fixed directions preserves mean PDC). It requires storing training response vectors and computing nearest-neighbor cosine distances per prediction, plus calibration data to set thresholds; the underlying model and decoder are unchanged, so no retraining or extra GPU capacity is needed. It can fail when predictions are reliable but far from all training responses (false low confidence), when the training set poorly covers the test distribution, and its validation is specific to the STATE ST decoder and CRISPRi/drug perturbation settings, so transfer to other architectures or assay types is unverified. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
item.description: MAEP replaces modality-agnostic expert-pruning importance metrics with a training-free, single-forward-pass metric that separates vision-side pruning signals from text-side preservation signals for MoE-based MLLMs. Cost is limited to a calibration forward pass and permanent removal of experts, with no retraining; inference speed is largely unchanged since it removes parameters rather than adding compute. It can fail when the workload's vision-token statistics differ from those used for calibration, when the low-attention vision-token assumption breaks on a new domain, or when text-heavy tasks suffer because text importance was only a preservation signal rather than the optimization target. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Phantom: Temporal Caching for Diffusion Models
item.description: Phantom replaces full diffusion computation by reusing cached activations and recomputing only tokens that change significantly between timesteps. The approach requires specialized systolic-array hardware additions, making it inaccessible to standard GPU or API deployments. The method may fail if outlier detection degrades image quality or if hardware-specific assumptions do not transfer to commodity accelerators. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SysPilot: Cross-Library Performance Autotuning via Library Performance Contracts
item.description: The method replaces application-specific manual tuning and general-purpose autotuners with reusable Library Performance Contracts that encode resource demands and observability signals across libraries. It requires contract synthesis from documentation and code artifacts plus profiling runs to validate conflict hypotheses, which adds specification and instrumentation complexity. It can fail when contracts are incomplete or inaccurate, when contention patterns shift across deployments, or when the target libraries lack sufficient observability to validate the derived hypotheses. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TauLang: A Language and Compiler for Space-Time Programming on Statically Scheduled Accelerators
item.description: TauLang replaces implicit, hardware-resolved scheduling in conventional kernel languages with explicit parameterized time annotations, validated algebraically and solved jointly with tensor placement via an integer linear program. The cost is a new language and compiler toolchain plus ILP solve time, and it presupposes a statically scheduled accelerator such as a Groq TSP rather than a GPU. It fails to apply when the target hardware has dynamic scheduling (caches, arbiters, hardware schedulers), and schedule validity depends on compiler correctness since mistimed operations are correctness errors, not performance regressions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Shallow Encoding Emits Deep Memories
item.description: The technique replaces full-depth prefill with a shallow emitter that writes deep-layer memories from an earlier anchor layer, and replaces full recurrent-state storage with a fixed sink direction plus low-rank factors. It keeps the original weights frozen and does not compress the attention cache, but requires hybrid architectures with recurrent states and support for exact low-rank state updates in the serving stack. Quality risk is bounded but real: the method is only validated on six checkpoints of production hybrids, and the throughput gain depends on workloads with long prompts or agentic traces. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FaCoDiff: Factor-Correlated Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting
item.description: Replaces dense covariance estimation or diagonal-noise diffusion models for multivariate probabilistic forecasting with a low-rank factor structure that preserves marginal variances while modeling cross-variable dependence. Costs include implementing a conditional statistical estimator, diagonal compensation mechanics, and a geometry-aware diffusion objective, though the method avoids O(N³) dense matrix operations. Can fail if the low-rank factor assumption does not capture true cross-variable dependence in your specific time series, or if the implementation complexity of the coupled estimator-denoiser introduces integration overhead disproportionate to accuracy gains over simpler baselines. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
item.description: The method replaces heuristic or random client selection in federated LoRA fine-tuning of multimodal LLMs with a Double Deep Q-Learning selector using Q-value decomposition, constraint-aware epsilon-greedy subset selection, and an adaptive aggregation rule that can upweight the previous global model. It costs the engineering complexity of running an online RL selector and per-round utility estimation on top of the federated orchestration, plus the overhead of tracking latency and bandwidth feasibility each round. It can fail if the online-learned utilities misestimate client value under shifting data or system conditions, if the emulated wireless setting does not transfer to real deployments, or if the adaptive aggregation stalls convergence by overweighting stale models. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
item.description: GEdit replaces unconstrained knowledge-editing methods (such as ROME/MEMIT-style weight updates and their sequential variants) with an LR+D factor model of FFN hidden representations that protects a low-rank core knowledge subspace and adapts regularization strength per edit difficulty. The cost is additional per-edit computation to estimate the representation geometry and calibrate editability, plus implementation complexity over existing editing libraries. It can fail if the assumed low-rank structure does not hold for a given model, if editability is miscalibrated (hard edits fail or easy edits corrupt pretrained knowledge), or if the method's benefits do not transfer beyond the evaluated GPT2-XL/GPT-J/LLaMA-3-8B settings. 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages
item.description: Replaces generative classification (prompting an LLM to output a label) with a fixed-set classifier that returns calibrated probabilities over options, trained via a low-rank adapter plus pointer head on frozen open-weight bases (4B, 9B, 27B). The 4B and 9B variants fit a 24 GB GPU for both adapter training and inference; costs are the adapter training pipeline, per-task calibration checks, and base-model dependence. Miscalibration varies by task (knowledge overconfident, acceptability underconfident) so no single temperature fixes all tasks; performance collapses 23-28 points in languages outside the base model's documented list, training data is vulnerable to label-word collisions and augmentation shortcuts, and English results lag competing models (Jev, Kev). 1 independent implementation, 129 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
item.description: This approach replaces sending proprietary code to hosted security-analysis APIs with locally-run open-weight models (4B–27B parameters) that autonomously generate crash-inducing inputs from vulnerability descriptions. The cost includes GPU memory sufficient for 27B-scale models (within 24 GB at appropriate quantization), slower wall-clock convergence compared to mixture-of-experts variants, and engineering effort to build execution harnesses that compile and run target code. Failure occurs when models correctly identify vulnerable functions and state hypotheses but cannot synthesize working exploit inputs, particularly on harder tasks where only 27B models succeed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code
item.description: The technique replaces default functionality-oriented context construction (standard retrieval, file ranking, agent-driven exploration) with security-aware context construction that explicitly surfaces safeguard code and excludes insecure exemplars before generation. It costs additional engineering to identify and annotate security-relevant repository elements per project, plus modest retrieval overhead, and provides no runtime latency change since it affects only context assembly. It can fail when safeguard locations are misidentified, when the model ignores injected safeguards, or when the security-relevant code is too dispersed across the repository to fit the context window. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MA-Mesh: Resilient Multi-Agent Collaboration via Role-based Self-Healing
item.description: This technique replaces ad-hoc output correction and static role assignment with a runtime self-healing layer that uses cross-agent reflection and dynamic role-based failover. It costs additional inference latency and token usage due to peer evaluation loops, alongside increased engineering complexity to synthesize and maintain executable policy code. The reflection mechanism can fail if agents reach consensus on incorrect outputs, and dynamic role reassignment may cause inconsistent behavior or infinite failover loops when integrated with unreliable third-party APIs. 2 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Where Should a KV-Cache Repair Budget Go? Distractor Structure and Contextual Compatibility in Non-Prefix Reuse
item.description: The method replaces full prefill of retrieved context with independent chunk-cache reuse plus a small repair budget spent on the answer-bearing chunk, preferentially by recomputing that chunk against the reused cache and placing it next to the question. It costs retriever dependence, extra orchestration to identify and move the target chunk, and workload-specific validation across models and datasets. It can fail when the retriever misses the target, when useful damage is spread across many similar chunks, and on dialogue-memory workloads where token-level selection remains competitive or better. 1 independent implementation, 125 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Zero-Shot Coordination among LLM Agents
item.description: Coordination-friendly definitions replace ad hoc prompts or bespoke shared scaffolding for independently developed LLM agents that must coordinate at test time. The cost is an added convention-discovery and prompt-specification step, with possible extra coordination overhead and dependence on the underlying LLM's reasoning quality. It can fail when the counterparty does not follow compatible definitions, when beliefs about the partner are wrong, or when the automatically discovered convention does not transfer to a new environment. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: D3D: Decoupled Diffusion Drafting for Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
item.description: Replaces target-conditioned draft models (e.g., EAGLE-style or DFlash drafters) that wait for target hidden states each round with a standalone blockwise diffusion drafter that drafts successor blocks during verification, overlapped in one packed pass. Costs include training the drafter with auxiliary autoregressive supervision, extra GPU memory to hold drafter and target concurrently on one device, and added serving complexity for asynchronous scheduling and packed drafting. Can fail if acceptance length degrades outside the reported benchmarks or after pruning, negating overlap gains, and the approach depends on the open-sourced implementation matching the paper's results on your specific target model and workload. 0 independent implementations, 134 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SUMONE: A Simple and Efficient Summarizer for Plug-and-Play Agent Memory
item.description: The method replaces full interaction-history prompting with a lightweight standalone summarizer trained via masked reconstruction and a GRPO reward, compressing expired agent history without task-specific training. It costs an additional small model to host or serve at inference time, plus GRPO training and a frozen reconstructor during development, and introduces a bounded quality loss (about 0.04 absolute on the reported benchmarks). It can fail when compressed trajectories discard details required for later steps, on workloads unlike the evaluated search and software-engineering tasks, or if the released checkpoint is unavailable or mismatched to the reader's agent harness. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: The method replaces trusting signatures plus cosine-tolerance recomputation of precomputed embeddings in offline RAG knowledge packs with verifier-controlled recomputation, quantisation-code verification, guard bands, and canonicalisation. It costs verifier-side embedding recomputation per update and added pipeline complexity for cross-platform canonicalisation, since common FP32 and dynamic-INT8 pipelines are not bit-reproducible across batch sizes and architectures. It can fail where deployment pipelines cannot be made deterministic enough to set a valid guard band, and abstention, context pruning, and semantic screening showed pre-registered negative results as alternative defences. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
item.description: Replaces raw textual tool observations appended to the agent's context with compressed latent tokens embedded directly in the model's input embedding space, trained via action-preserving alignment. Costs include training a dedicated compression model, modifying the agent's input pipeline to accept continuous latent tokens, and coupling to specific agent model families, which limits portability across API-only backends. Can fail when compressed observations omit decision-critical details outside the training distribution, and the approach is inapplicable to closed third-party APIs that do not expose input embedding access. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation
item.description: Replaces prefix-incremental generation and external Voice Activity Detection in simultaneous speech translation with an end-to-end interleaved read-write framework using an omni-modal LLM. Requires training an RNN-T Actor and LLM-based Critic, likely involving significant compute for policy distillation, and modifies the inference loop to handle unbounded streams. Infinite-length streaming stability and policy convergence may fail under distribution shift, and the Actor-Critic pipeline introduces training complexity compared to static alignment baselines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Trace2Eval: Contextualized Evaluation of Coding Agents from Real-World Traces
item.description: Trace2Eval replaces static benchmarks built on public tasks with reference patches or hidden tests by reconstructing executable evaluation tasks from real coding-agent interaction traces and scoring artifacts with human-calibrated judge agents. The cost is a substantial multi-agent pipeline — trajectory filtering, query reconstruction, workspace restoration, environment rebuilding, iterative rubric alignment, and judge calibration — plus the compute and annotation effort to keep it continually renewed, which is non-trivial for a small team. Failure modes include inaccurate reconstruction of the original query or workspace, judge miscalibration drifting from human assessment, rubric overfitting to observed traces, and feedback loops that improve rubric scores without improving real-world artifact quality. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Nowcasting Future Performance for Population Pruning in Survival-of-the-Fittest Training
item.description: The method replaces naive early-stopping rules (pruning by current accuracy) in population-based training with learned predictors that forecast final test accuracy from checkpoint features (weight statistics, SANE latent tokens), terminating low-ranked candidates early. It costs training an auxiliary nowcaster (and optionally a transformer autoencoder for SANE embeddings) plus periodic checkpoint analysis, and in homogeneous zoos it adds little over the free baseline of pruning by current accuracy. It can fail when the nowcaster is trained on a model zoo unrepresentative of the reader's architectures or hyperparameter distribution, when learning curves cross in ways the predictor misses, and it presupposes budget to train multiple candidates in parallel. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment
item.description: ORSD replaces sparse trajectory-level GRPO advantage with token-level credit obtained by generating natural-language process rubrics from groups of on-policy trajectories, verifying them against outcomes, and shaping advantages by the log-likelihood gap with and without the rubric. It costs additional inference passes for rubric generation and frozen-verifier evaluation at every training step, plus the complexity of running and tuning a multi-stage pipeline beyond vanilla GRPO. It can fail if the self-generated rubrics are noisy or misaligned with true task success, if the frozen verifier selects poorly correlated bundles, or if the method's benefits do not transfer beyond the demonstrated small models and text-agent benchmarks to the reader's domain. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries
item.description: The method replaces generic approval instructions (e.g., 'Some actions need approval') in agent system prompts with provenance guidance stating where requirements originate, preventing the agent from hallucinating unsupported permissions in self-written context summaries. It costs only a system prompt modification—no additional infrastructure, memory, or latency overhead. Failure modes include residual unsupported restrictions (0.3% held-out rate) and fragile mitigation of unsupported authorizations, which showed inconsistent effects across held-out sets (17 to 11 of 48 runs). 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: EPISTEME: Trustworthy Coding Agents Through Tool Call Intent
item.description: The method replaces un-audited tool execution in coding agents with a harness that forces the model to declare intent before each tool call, records actual effects, and checks declaration against effects to produce a journal usable for pre-execution guards and post-hoc forensics. It costs extra structured output per call, harness engineering to capture and diff state changes, and added latency from gating checks, with negligible GPU or training requirements since it wraps existing models. It can fail if the model fabricates plausible intents that match surface effects while hiding side effects, if effect capture is incomplete, or if the guard logic is too weak to act on mismatches. 0 independent implementations, 2114 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information
item.description: The method replaces adapter quality assessment via rank, parameter count, or reconstruction error with an operational compression-based behavioral rate, and replaces discarding noise-corrupted fine-tunes with post-training adapter compression that filters corrupted leading singular directions. It costs a compression-and-reload step plus held-out evaluation per adapter, with no extra inference latency, but requires empirical calibration of the retained-gain threshold per model–dataset pair. It can fail because the behavioral rate is specific to the dataset–receiver pair and does not transfer across base models, and the noise-filtering benefit has only been demonstrated on limited task families and corruption settings. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Policy, Grounding, and Trajectory Tests for Java LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces ad hoc or purely infrastructure-level security checks with deterministic build-time JUnit tests over recorded agent traces that verify tool policy, grounding, and workflow trajectory. It costs the effort of authoring behavioral expectations, maintaining them as workflows evolve, and recording or replaying traces, plus optional LLM-judge API spend if semantic evaluation is enabled. It can fail because all evidence comes from a synthetic corpus with deliberately isolated faults, so real production traces may expose missed fault classes, and expectations can silently drift from actual workflow changes. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Airlock: Bounding the Multi-Agent Blast Radius via Selective Online Containment
item.description: Airlock replaces binary multi-agent fault handling (cancel-source-only or full halt-and-rollback) with selective post-alert containment using a tree-structured permission runtime (EdgeCitadel) and an append-only provenance DAG to trace and isolate tainted executions. It costs the engineering complexity of deploying a custom runtime with hierarchical permission narrowing and continuous provenance tracking across all agent interactions, plus potential latency from the fence-then-prune minimum-cut computation under deadline constraints. It can fail if the initial alert itself is delayed or missed (containment is post-alert, not preventive), if the provenance DAG has gaps in tracking cross-agent data flows, or if the permission boundaries are misconfigured and either over-isolate healthy work or under-isolate tainted branches. 2 independent implementations, 2124 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Continual Classification Beyond the Kernel Regime: Harnessing the Sparsity Bias of L2 Regularization in Diagonal Linear Networks
item.description: Replaces conventional L2 or L1 regularization centered on previous-task weights in continual linear/diagonal-network classification with a weighted L2 variant designed to preserve the sparsity bias of deep linear models. Costs are limited to implementing the per-weight weighting and accepting some long-horizon bias relative to standard continual L2. Can fail if the underlying teacher is not sufficiently sparse, since the claimed speed and accuracy advantage depends on that sparsity. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Enabling AWS Cloud FPGA Development Using High-Level Vitis HLS
item.description: The toolchain replaces hand-written HDL/RTL development for AWS EC2 F2 FPGA instances with a Vitis HLS C++-to-AFI workflow plus a four-level debugging methodology. It costs substantial hardware engineering effort, HLS-to-FPGA timing closure work, and the paper's own deployment streams weights from host DRAM and reports poor performance compared with CPU/GPU implementations. It can fail through timing-closure problems, FPGA-specific circuit errors, and throughput that remains uncompetitive unless on-chip weight storage or memory architecture is redesigned. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
item.description: ServerBench replaces manual, expert-driven tuning of LLM serving stacks with a benchmark in which coding agents design, test, and verify complete specialized serving systems against a dollars-per-dollar objective. It costs agent API spend, GPU time for experimentation, and the added verification and stateful-replay infrastructure; only about two-thirds of runs yield verified systems. After adoption, agent-generated optimizations can introduce execution-path bugs that break correctness or session dependencies unless independently verified, and results may not transfer across workloads or deployments. 2 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc or non-expert evaluation of multi-reference image generation with a graph-grounded, checklist-based benchmark that audits entity-relation fidelity and constraint satisfaction. Costs include integrating the 90-task harness, managing ~32 reference images per task, and orchestrating the RPR workflow if using LongBanana-Gen. Evaluation may fail if expert labels are domain-specific or if the 15% double-labeled subset does not generalize to the reader's visual domain. 3 independent implementations, 161 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
item.description: The study replaces manual, expert-designed LLM compression pipelines (quantization, format conversion, inference code) with a terminal-based coding agent that autonomously searches compression strategies under a storage and time budget. Adopting this approach costs agent compute and wall-clock time for iterative experiments, plus a 3.4% perplexity increase and roughly a 2.2-point downstream accuracy drop relative to BF16. Failures include misleading local likelihood rankings (17 of 79 reversed by complete-model feedback) and generation or inference defects that perplexity verification alone does not detect. 2 independent implementations, 137 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
item.description: This replaces storing full-precision, full-dimensionality embedding vectors (float32 at native dimension) with int8-quantized, dimensionally truncated hierarchical embeddings. The cost is at most roughly 1.5 percentage points of effectiveness overall and a small integration effort to emit and store shorter quantized vectors, with no measured evaluation speedup from quantization itself. It can fail on retrieval tasks, which degrade far faster than other categories, and binary quantization or two successive dimension halvings are significantly worse and should not be adopted. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: GH-AWTrace: A Large-Scale Dataset of GitHub Agentic Workflow Execution Logs
item.description: GH-AWTrace replaces the reliance on workflow definitions and final run outcomes by providing a linked dataset of 25,014 GitHub Agentic Workflows, 4.1M run records, and 562,877 nonempty execution-log archives for studying what happens during execution. It costs no model deployment, but using it requires data engineering to parse partial logs, repository metadata, and generated workflow configurations under GitHub log-retention limits. It can fail as a production guide because coverage varies across workflows and the logs are partial observations rather than complete agent trajectories. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces single-sample action generation in agent loops with a generator-selector scheme: at each turn one model proposes N candidate actions and a second model picks one before execution. The cost is roughly N+1 model calls per turn instead of one, multiplying latency and API expenditure linearly with N and adding a selection step whose quality bounds the gain. It can fail when the off-the-shelf selector cannot reliably rank candidate actions for a given domain, when tasks are short enough that per-turn overhead dominates, or when poor candidates are executed because the selector's errors compound over long horizons. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
item.description: The method replaces sequential, single-pass large-model summarization of agent interaction histories with parallel drafting of structured summary slots by a fine-tuned small model, which the target model then verifies line-by-line and repairs where needed. Costs include training and maintaining the drafter model, additional system complexity for parallel generation and verification orchestration, and potential quality trade-offs that the paper notes are model- and task-dependent. The approach can fail when the small drafter produces low-quality slot proposals that the target model must extensively repair, reducing or negating speedup, or when downstream task performance degrades due to information loss from aggressive or inaccurate compaction. 2 independent implementations, 135 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MCP-Eco: A Linked Dataset of MCP Servers, Consumers, and Development Activity
item.description: MCP-Eco replaces ad hoc scraping of MCP directories, registries, and repository histories with a frozen relational dataset of servers, consumers, configurations, and development activity. It costs storage and query capacity for 16.9M Parquet records plus integration effort, with no direct runtime overhead unless used in production analysis. It can fail if snapshot staleness, imperfect declaration matching, or provenance ambiguity misrepresents current MCP interfaces and dependencies. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
item.description: FrontierPhysics replaces fixed-question and isolated sub-task physics benchmarks with 56 end-to-end research tasks graded by deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics; it is an evaluation suite, not a deployable method, so it replaces nothing in the reader's production stack. Adopting it costs expert-level task authoring or access to the benchmark, plus compute to run full research rollouts (literature review, planning, experimentation, manuscript writing), which is substantial per rollout. It can fail as a decision tool because rubric-based grading involves subjective expert judgment, 56 tasks limit statistical power, and benchmark rankings may not transfer to the reader's actual agent workload. 3 independent implementations, 2249 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
item.description: The framework replaces informal prompt-sensitivity checks for LLM-based social simulation agents with systematic context-enrichment substitution rules (neutral padding, social background, descriptive and normative grounding) evaluated against a selective robustness criterion: invariance to meaning-preserving prompt changes plus directional sensitivity to decision-relevant changes. Cost is additional prompt engineering and multiplied evaluation runs across variants and models; it uses existing API or single-GPU inference, so no new infrastructure is required, but the token cost of enriched contexts rises with prompt length. Results are model-dependent—the two tested models showed distinct behavioral patterns—so enrichment choices validated on one model may not transfer, and findings demonstrated in a Prisoner's Dilemma-like game may not generalize to other simulation settings. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: OSGR: Observation-Support Graph Reasoning for Earth Observation Question Answering
item.description: OSGR replaces unconstrained LLM-agent search over Earth observation archives with a two-stage factorization: an offline Observation-Support Graph deduces valid concept-level support paths, and online Relation-Conditioned Grounding instantiates items under spatiotemporal compatibility kernels. The cost is building and maintaining the offline symbolic graph plus a domain-specific grounding pipeline, which is engineering effort orthogonal to general-purpose workloads. It can fail where the offline graph lacks coverage of required concepts or relations, and its gains are demonstrated only on EO benchmarks, so transfer to other retrieval-and-derivation domains is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Drift No More: Spectral Locking for Long-Horizon Open-Weight Multi-Agent AI
item.description: ATLAS replaces surface-text interventions (prompting, retrieval, external memory modules) for controlling task, role, and state drift with training-free steering of hidden states toward joint task-role-state eigendirections at inference time. It costs hidden-state access on every generated token (so it applies only to open-weight models, not third-party APIs), plus per-agent anchor subspace computation via a low-rank Gram decomposition, adding modest latency and engineering complexity. It can fail if the anchor subspaces are misspecified for a given workload, if the reported benchmarks do not transfer to the reader's task distribution, or if the representational-drift hypothesis does not hold on a different backbone. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ATC: Agent Trajectory Control for Role-Contract Enforcement in Black-Box Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: ATC replaces implicit role separation via prompting or fixed workflow graphs with an explicit per-role contract and a gate that scores each proposed message for out-of-role deviation, leakage into other roles' functions, impermissible speech acts, and contract breaches, then constrains regeneration and re-checks before admission. It costs an additional scoring-and-possible-regeneration step per message, adding latency and API or GPU inference calls on every turn, plus the engineering burden of authoring and maintaining role contracts. It can fail through misclassification of legitimate cross-role messages (blocking useful behavior or looping regenerations), poorly specified contracts, and dependence on a scorer whose own reliability bounds the enforcement quality. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CloakFEM: Agentic FEM Code Generation for Red-Teaming Computational Resource Exhaustion
item.description: This technique replaces manual or generic black-box fuzzing for FEM solver efficiency attacks with a domain-guided LLM-agent that generates runnable adversarial programs. It requires specialized FEM-domain infrastructure, an intermediate representation, and a deterministic validity gate, with costs in implementation complexity and domain expertise. The method can fail if applied to general LLM inference workloads or if the agent's search misses edge cases in untested FEM configurations. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Do Coding Agents Follow AGENTS.md? The Effect of Policy Wording on Instruction Compliance
item.description: The technique replaces unexamined or default policy wording in AGENTS.md-style context files with deliberately chosen phrasing styles, such as Prescriptive or Explanatory, to improve instruction compliance. It costs only authoring and prompt-maintenance effort, with negligible infrastructure overhead, but requires per-setup validation because the best wording was not stable across harness-model combinations. It can fail if a team standardizes on one style that performs worse for their specific agent stack or if improved wording still does not yield reliable policy adherence on real tasks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Aligning Training and Rollout Policies for End-to-End FP4 RL on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
item.description: MoeResQ replaces asymmetric FP4 recovery recipes for MoE RL post-training, including the dense-model approach that applies correction only on the rollout side, with a symmetric recipe that applies the same correction to both training and inference. Its cost is the additional engineering of maintaining identical quantization-recovery logic on both sides of the RL loop, plus the compute of FP4 RL post-training itself. It can fail if the two correction paths drift out of symmetry in implementation, since router discrete expert selection makes alignment acutely sensitive to any asymmetry, and the abstract provides no evidence for dense models or for inference-only serving workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Beyond Compression Ratio: High-Throughput KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving
item.description: The method replaces a multi-stage KV compression pipeline (separate distribution transform, low-bit quantization, and a proprietary lossless backend) with a fused TileLang kernel and an open LC-based compression backend for disaggregated serving. The cost is implementation complexity: it depends on the KVServe disaggregated serving stack, custom TileLang kernels, and the LC library, none of which are drop-in components of standard single-GPU inference frameworks. It can fail when the serving setup is not disaggregated (no KV transfer over a network, so no communication savings to preserve), when interconnect bandwidth is low enough that compression overhead dominates, or when workload-specific KV distributions reduce the achievable compression throughput. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Disposable Implementations: What Is Software Engineering For?
item.description: The paper proposes that coding agents replace incremental maintenance of existing codebases with routine regeneration of clean implementations from preserved requirements, tests, architectural constraints, and operational records. The cost shifts from code maintenance to maintaining the specification artifacts, verification processes, and continuity mechanisms that make regeneration trustworthy. The principal failure mode is silent behavioral loss: a regenerated implementation may pass available tests while dropping undocumented safeguards, failure-driven fixes, and implicit assumptions embedded only in the old code. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Voluntary Servitude: Weaponized Safety Warning Mechanisms for Controlling AI Agents
item.description: The technique replaces reliance on instruction-injection detectors, which miss attacks that steer agents through fabricated safety hazards rather than command syntax; it consists of adding an instruction requiring the agent to corroborate retrieved hazard claims before acting on them. The cost is negligible: a system-prompt change with no retraining, no extra infrastructure, and only minor latency from the agent seeking corroborating sources. It can fail against adaptive attackers who fabricate multiple corroborating sources, and it does not address other injection vectors, so it must be combined with existing defenses rather than substituted for them. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Silent Instrument Errors Reorder Agent Leaderboards
item.description: Replaces implicit trust in leaderboard scores and their underlying evaluation pipelines with explicit auditing of grading, logging, replay, and versioning artifacts, plus adopting four cheap checks (graded fraction, root-span cost aggregation, action provenance tagging, pinned evaluator versions with re-grade diffs). Costs are primarily engineering time to implement reporting and provenance tracking and occasional re-grading compute; no foundation-model training or cluster is required. Failure after adoption includes residual silent instrumentation bugs elsewhere, misinterpretation of published diffs or provenance, and re-grading itself becoming a new, unacknowledged measurement if versions and procedures are not pinned. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SWAP-INR: Implicit Neural Representation with Switchable Attention Paths for Time-varying Multivariate Scientific Data Compression
item.description: This method replaces traditional lossy compressors and standard implicit neural representations (INRs) for time-varying multivariate scientific simulation data. It costs the engineering effort of training a specialized architecture and requires post-training 16-bit quantization to maintain a constrained memory footprint. It can fail when applied to data lacking the specific cross-variable interactions of physics simulations, or when deployment targets lack support for the custom attention-based decoding process. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Sketchpad: certified exact arithmetic with a small vision-language model
item.description: The method replaces both unverified in-network arithmetic (sampled accuracy with no per-input guarantee) and calculator-style tool calls, by having a small adapted model execute procedures step-by-step on a rendered external sheet whose correctness over a finite view set is machine-checked. It costs a custom training adapter, a dedicated rendering and runtime stack, formal verification effort, and many sequential forward passes per operation, so latency scales with problem length far worse than a single tool call. Adoption fails if any of the finite views fails certification on the deployment quantization, if workloads need operations outside the verified procedure set, or if the added per-step inference latency outweighs the value of in-network exactness over calling a calculator. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product
item.description: SaMA replaces standard LoRA adapters with a generalized Kronecker product parameterization that relaxes the shared-block constraint, achieving effective rank scaling quadratically with parameter budget up to full rank. It costs no additional inference latency (adapters merge like LoRA) but requires implementing a new factorization and tuning rank/allocation hyperparameters; memory overhead depends on chosen rank configuration. The diagonal invariance group is claimed to improve optimization geometry, but adoption can fail if the quadratic rank scaling does not materialize on the target task or if implementation complexity outweighs gains over well-tuned LoRA. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Watching to Steering: Enabling Human-Coding Agent Collaboration through Execution Traces
item.description: It replaces conventional log-based interaction and full run restarts with interactive execution-trace visualization, mid-run forking, and distillation of traces plus human feedback into reusable skills. It costs a custom instrumentation and UI layer built on OpenCode, ongoing human supervision time, and added system complexity. It can fail if distilled skills overfit to past tasks, if traces become too long to inspect reliably on long runs, or if forked executions diverge from validated state in subtle ways. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization
item.description: The method replaces ad-hoc signal-to-text serialization or raw feature injection by mapping four-step signal patches to a 625-code discrete vocabulary via a frozen finite-scalar-quantization tokenizer, letting a pretrained LLM process signal tokens, scale statistics, and text jointly with standard self-attention. It costs training a context-aware Transformer tokenizer, extending the embedding matrix, and task-specific fine-tuning with DoRA adapters on a 4B-parameter backbone, which fits within a single 24 GB GPU for inference but adds tokenizer training and fine-tuning complexity. It can fail when the frozen tokenizer's quantization loses signal fidelity on out-of-distribution series, when the 625-code vocabulary under-represents high-frequency dynamics, and when task-specific fine-tuning does not transfer across domains or sensor configurations. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SKILL2STEER: One-Pass Hypernetwork for Mapping Natural-Language Skills to Low-Rank Post-Block Activation Shifts
item.description: It replaces keeping natural-language skill instructions in the prompt (and, relative to per-skill weight adapters, replaces weight-space adaptation) by compiling a skill document once into low-rank post-block activation shifts while keeping base weights frozen and running the hypernetwork only at compile time. It costs an additional compile-time hypernetwork pass plus a small per-skill artifact (2.36M parameters) and requires integrating activation-shift injection at every decoder block (optionally scheduled across retrieval steps), with routing-free deployment possible as a single averaged bundle. It can fail because the learned shift may encode a domain-general behavioural prior rather than the skill content (wrong skill text can perform on par), so behaviour can change without delivering the intended skill-specific semantics and may be sensitive to domain shift, scheduling, and deployment details. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FreeForm Harness: A Mobile-Native Agent Harness for Open and Composable Extensions
item.description: Replaces monolithic mobile-agent pipelines with a frozen base and uniform plugin contract so independently authored extensions can be published, installed, composed, checked, and replaced. Costs include platform engineering across device, market, and cloud, runtime validation overhead, and operational exposure to generated extension code. It can fail through plugin incompatibilities, incorrect intent-to-extension retrieval, unsafe commissioned artifacts, or unusable user experiences when location, proactive triggers, or scarce channels are mishandled. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Exploiting Biases in Attention for Transformers
item.description: The technique modifies the standard query-key dot product in self-attention by adding an input-dependent bias term that explicitly scores token importance independently of specific queries, enabling pruning of attention map columns to reduce computation. It requires a reformulated attention mechanism and incurs the cost of computing these biases while accepting a trade-off where some original classification accuracy is lost in exchange for reduced FLOPs and latency. Failure modes include potential degradation in tasks requiring dense attention patterns, risks associated with pruning based on anticipated rather than actual token influence, and the need for task-specific validation to determine acceptable accuracy-latency trade-offs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library for Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing
item.description: The library replaces explicit construction of the global sparse sheaf Laplacian with local incidence-wise transport and aggregation in PyTorch Geometric, reducing memory and implementation overhead. The cost is adopting a specialized graph-learning library and sheaf-based model families rather than standard GNN tooling, with added architectural and benchmarking complexity. It can fail to deliver practical benefit if the target workload does not involve heterophilic or heterogeneous graphs, or if the claimed scalability gains do not hold for the reader's graph sizes and task mix. 1 independent implementation, 25 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LeanSparse: Memory-Efficient Serving for Native Sparse-Attention LLMs
item.description: LeanSparse replaces full on-GPU retention of indexer keys and monolithic prefill memory allocation in sparse-attention serving with layer-by-layer streamed prefill through reusable buffers and coarse-to-fine candidate retrieval over compact index representations. The cost is systems complexity: a modified SGLang runtime, separate indexer-key and KV caches, and dependency on models with native sparse attention (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash), so the gains do not transfer to standard dense-attention models. It can fail if the coarse index pruning degrades retrieval quality for some workloads, if the implementation remains tied to a specific serving stack, or if the reader's actual context lengths are far below the regime where memory pressure justifies the added machinery. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries
item.description: Replaces the need for every project to build custom extraction pipelines to convert MIMIC-IV free-text discharge summaries into structured tables. Costs are low for the reader because the output is a pre-computed dataset; the authors absorbed the LLM inference and engineering expense, though integrating a new schema requires effort. Schema-guided LLM extraction can hallucinate or misclassify clinical entities, and the 8% error rate may require manual verification for high-stakes applications. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
item.description: It replaces iterative diffusion or flow-matching sampling for probabilistic time-series forecasting with Koopman-patch latent extrapolation, a closed-form matrix-exponential single-step generator, and an adaptive per-variable/per-horizon uncertainty gate. The cost is added model and implementation complexity, dependence on learning a stable Koopman latent representation, and likely retraining or integration work rather than drop-in use on an existing forecasting stack. It can fail if the learned linear latent dynamics poorly approximate strongly nonlinear or regime-switching series, if the closed-form generation becomes unstable over longer horizons, or if the reported gains do not transfer from benchmark data to the reader's workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Replica-Aware Split Inference for Edge IoT Systems
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc or greedy replica re-hosting of TinyML model segments after an IoT device failure with a MILP formulation that jointly selects replica hosts and communication protocols to minimize post-reconfiguration latency under memory constraints. The cost is solving a mixed-integer linear program at recovery time, which requires centralized knowledge of the network state and adds solver latency and orchestration complexity to the failure-recovery path. It can fail if link rates or device capabilities drift from the modeled values used by the optimizer, if solver time exceeds the tolerable recovery window, or if flash and runtime memory on surviving devices is insufficient for the chosen replicas. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Training Specialist LLMs on Your Phone: Forward-Only Optimization via Block-Spectral Coordinates
item.description: MobileSpec replaces backpropagation-based fine-tuning and full-parameter evolution strategies with forward-only training that rescales block-spectral coordinates (singular values of column blocks) of pretrained weights, enabling RLVR-style learning from verifiable rewards without labeled data. It requires only forward passes, produces 1-5 MB specialist adapters touching 0.015-0.05% of parameters, and can adapt INT4 quantized models without modifying their weights, but it depends on automatically verifiable task outcomes rather than general supervised data. It can fail when task rewards cannot be automatically verified, when forward-only perturbation efficiency degrades outside the validated regimes, or when on-device overnight training assumptions (e.g., 8B on an iPhone 16 Pro) do not transfer to the reader's hardware and workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
item.description: BP-TD replaces plain majority vote and classical Dawid-Skene crowdsourcing estimators for combining conflicting answers from multiple LLM agents by adding per-agent decorrelation weights so that agents sharing a base model count as roughly one vote. It costs only mean-field variational inference over a one-coin model, which is computationally trivial on constrained infrastructure, but it requires maintaining a multi-agent pool whose members are meaningfully diverse rather than variants of one model. It can fail when the largest correlated bloc is actually the strongest agent group, in which case decorrelation hurts accuracy, and the authors report no label-free statistic that distinguishes this case from the favorable one. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud
item.description: ScamWorld replaces ad hoc or live-web testing of web agents against online fraud, which is impractical because real scam sites are short-lived, with a controlled, repeatable suite of reconstructed scam websites exposing observable fraud signals before the agent's final action. The cost is environment setup, maintenance of reconstructed scenarios, and evaluation compute across agent trajectories, with added complexity in keeping reconstructed fraud mechanisms current as real scams evolve. It can fail through overfitting to the reproduced scenarios, underrepresenting novel fraud patterns, and producing results that do not transfer to live web conditions. 3 independent implementations, 2244 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FourSight: Stable FP4 RL Post-Training via Sequence Filtering and Sparse Channel Compensation
item.description: FourSight replaces naive NVFP4 W4A4 quantization in RL post-training by combining TIM-aware sequence filtering to exclude drifted trajectories with sparse precision compensation that keeps only high-variance activation channels in BF16, plus a fused SpliceGEMM kernel. The method adds kernel complexity and requires engine-specific implementation for the fused prefill/decode datapaths, with step time within 2.3% of baseline FP4. Severely mismatched tail tokens may still evade filtering if the outlier concentration assumption does not hold for a given model or task, and the approach targets models at scales (up to 120B) that exceed the reader's 24 GB GPU capacity. 1 independent implementation, 124 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
item.description: VisSearch-Bench replaces ad hoc or text-centric evaluation of multimodal search agents with 204 human-written tasks (plus reference answers, traceable evidence, and process scoring) that stress visual context management across set-wise, sequential, hybrid, disambiguation, and structure-guided search. Adoption costs nothing in compute beyond running your own agent against the tasks, but it requires API or inference budget to execute multi-step image-plus-web search trajectories and human or scripted scoring against its rules. It can fail as a proxy if your production workload does not involve linking visual evidence to external search results, since strong or weak scores here may not transfer to simpler entity-identification-plus-text-retrieval tasks. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PROSE: Preservation-Constrained Selective Editing for Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction
item.description: PROSE replaces retraining or generic fine-tuning for removing a specific verdict bias by reconstructing case-specific intervention targets from a residual geometry and applying a preservation-regularized low-rank parameter update, leaving standard single-pass inference unchanged. The cost is a legally reviewed matched-pair dataset, held-out activation-intervention analysis, and added editing pipeline complexity rather than inference overhead. Target-reaching interventions can damage supported-guilty decisions, so repairs may trade one error class for another and may not transfer outside the studied charges and models. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning
item.description: M2LE replaces single scalar-coefficient LoRA merging after each continual-learning task with an element-wise modulation of the LoRA update derived from a Hessian-guided joint loss over previous and current tasks, plus a perturbation-based task-interference simulation during training. The cost is additional computation: Hessian (or Hessian-vector-product) estimation and an analytic solve per task, plus extra perturbation training steps, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU but adding complexity to the fine-tuning loop. What can fail is Hessian approximation quality on small compute budgets, sensitivity of the analytic solution to noisy second-order estimates, and the fact that the method only applies if the reader's workload is sequential multi-task fine-tuning with LoRA adapters. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: GeoFaham: Domain-Specialized Multi-Agent Geospatial Analytics for Disaster Response
item.description: Replaces general-purpose coding agents with specialist geospatial agents coordinated by an orchestrator using a dual-ledger control loop and an external Response Store for artifacts. Costs include building and maintaining multiple specialist agents, geospatial tool integrations, and state-management infrastructure beyond a single agent loop. Can fail when tasks fall outside the disaster-geospatial domain, when underlying data sources or raster pipelines are unavailable, or when orchestration overhead outweighs gains on simpler tasks. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: ToolSpace replaces data-centric MCP environment synthesis (where databases and scenarios are invented first and tools derived from them, producing mismatched interfaces and ungrounded compositions) with a tool-centric pipeline that mines dependencies from real execution traces using deterministic rules, replays recorded returns for stateless tools, and keeps only tasks that replay successfully. Costs include the need for execution traces from real MCP services or open agent corpora, engineering effort to build the weighted tool-composition graph, state-aware random walks with rollback, and assertion-based validation, plus ongoing maintenance of the synthesized databases for state-mutating environments. It can fail if available traces are sparse or unrepresentative of the reader's production tools, if recorded returns become stale as real services change, or if the deterministic dependency mining misses implicit couplings that LLM judgment would catch. 3 independent implementations, 2272 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Gated Spec-Driven Workflow: An Audit-Trail Study of Coding-Agent Work
item.description: Replaces freeform chat-transcript-driven coding agents with a staged specification-plan-task workflow where a reviewer subagent checks artefacts against fixed defect lists, an executor is restricted to declared files, and a file-inventory check runs after each task block. Costs are human approval at every stage, orchestration overhead, and reliance on the same model to both enforce and obey constraints. The main failure mode is the orchestrator judging its own checks: it logged undeclared changes in 11 of 247 block checks but halted work in only four, so enforcement can silently weaken. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
item.description: The method replaces manual scripting and model-specific queries with a natural-language LLM agent that calls CFD-trained surrogate tools via MCP to predict spatter, melt-pool geometry, defect regimes, and run constrained process-window optimization. It adds LLM/API inference cost, agent orchestration complexity, and dependence on a validated surrogate and tool schemas, rather than eliminating the need for simulation data or domain validation. It can fail through incorrect tool parameterization, surrogate extrapolation outside the calibrated power-velocity range, residual geometry misclassification near defect boundaries, and overconfident optimization if process drift or model error is underestimated. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Provably Learning Mixtures of Linear Experts
item.description: The paper provides a convergence analysis for jointly training gates and linear experts via gradient EM, replacing heuristic MoE training practice with a characterized recipe: logarithmic overparameterization relative to the true expert count, random gate initialization, and unconstrained mixing weights that concentrate routing so the model can later be pruned. It costs nothing to read but addresses a canonical linear-expert model under Gaussian input clusters and a separation condition, not the deep nonlinear MoE architectures used in production. The global convergence guarantee fails if clusters are not separated, and the analysis is asymptotic in character, so its predictions may not transfer to small-data, non-Gaussian, or deep-expert regimes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Parallel Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics in Python: Task- and Data-Parallel SINDy with Numba, OpenMP, Threads and Multiprocessing for the Lorenz and Rössler Systems
item.description: The method replaces PySINDy's interpreted library evaluation and least-squares solves with Numba-JIT loop kernels that accumulate normal equations in a cache-blocked pass, parallelized via prange, PyOMP, threads, or multiprocessing. It costs implementation and maintenance of custom compiled kernels plus a QR fallback path for ill-conditioned problems, and its 117x figure was measured on a 24-core dual-socket HPC node, not commodity hardware. It can fail numerically when normal equations are ill-conditioned (mitigated by the QR fallback) and the exact-coefficient guarantee is demonstrated only on the Lorenz and Rössler benchmarks, not on noisy or large-scale real data. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models
item.description: Replaces standard unregularized maximum-likelihood or adversarial training of implicit generative models with a scoring-rule posterior combined with shrinkage priors and block SGMCMC within Gibbs sampling to induce sparsity. Costs include substantial implementation complexity (custom MCMC within Gibbs, scoring-rule posterior construction) and higher per-iteration compute than standard SGD, without a stated reduction in inference-time memory or latency. Can fail because the abstract offers no evidence the method transfers to production-scale architectures or standard data-regime sizes, MCMC convergence is difficult to diagnose in high dimensions, and sparsity may degrade sample quality. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
item.description: LoopVQ replaces per-step full-precision KV cache storage in looped transformers with joint vector quantization of channels across loop steps, using codebooks fine-tuned to match full-precision outputs. It costs a codebook fine-tuning stage, integration with a specific serving stack (SGLang implementation provided), and some residual accuracy loss that grows as bitrate drops toward 0.25 bits, where it must be combined with TaSQ to stay near BF16. It can fail if the deployed model is not a looped transformer (the method exploits redundancy along the loop axis, which standard LLMs lack), if loop-step sensitivity estimates do not transfer across tasks, or if codebook fine-tuning data does not cover the target distribution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
item.description: Replaces direct on-policy self-distillation over raw, noisy skill memories with a multi-view scheme that splits skills into state-grounding, action-planning, and execution-control branches, filters them with dynamic quality metrics, and consolidates them into one policy. Cost is primarily training-time complexity: maintaining and filtering three view-specific branches, plus the underlying RL and OPSD loop, which requires policy training capacity that a single 24 GB GPU can only handle for small models; inference cost is claimed unchanged. Failure modes include misclassification of skills into views, dynamic metric filtering that retains noisy or drops useful skills, and degraded performance when memory quality is low, an issue the paper itself identifies under limited training budgets. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
item.description: The method replaces human teleoperation for collecting robot demonstration data with a coding agent that rebuilds the task in simulation, generates expert actions, and renders photorealistic videos via a video model, charging roughly $21 per task setup plus $0.80 per episode. Costs are API usage, a $5 render contract, and dependence on an external simulator, video model, and judge ensemble rather than on local GPU or cluster resources. It can fail if the simulator, video model, or judges are unavailable or too expensive, if the reconstructed scene or controller does not match real dynamics, or if judge certification passes low-quality episodes that degrade the trained policy. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Accelerating LLM Pretraining with Zeroth-Order Curvature on Idle Serving Compute
item.description: ZO-Curv replaces the standard AdamW pretraining update with a curvature-adapted first-order update, where curvature is estimated by forward-only zeroth-order queries dispatched to idle inference-serving hardware that would otherwise sit unused. The cost is a heterogeneous training-and-serving orchestration layer, finite-query curvature estimation noise, and the need for serving devices that can run the model's forward pass while a separate training node performs first-order steps. The approach can fail when insufficient idle serving compute is available, when noisy curvature estimates mislead the update at small query budgets, or when the operational complexity of co-scheduling training and serving outweighs the wall-clock gain. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GraTED: Graph--Tensor EEG Decoding for Passenger Hazard Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
item.description: GraTED replaces 2D-grid CNN-style EEG classifiers with graph convolutions over electrode scalp geometry plus low-rank tensor classification of time-feature representations. The cost is a specialized preprocessing and modeling pipeline (electrode-graph construction, tensor decomposition) and a task-specific architecture rather than a general-purpose component. It can fail to generalize beyond the small 11-subject dataset, requires EEG hardware and AV hazard-label infrastructure the reader likely lacks, and offers no quantified accuracy margin over baselines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. Multi-Layer Perceptrons: A Rigorous Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data
item.description: KAN variants replace the tuned MLP as the classifier on structured clinical tabular data. They cost 1.20x-1.48x more inference latency and up to 12.5x more parameters, with no systematic pooled accuracy advantage. Gains are confined to severely imbalanced cohorts (minority-class AUPRC), so adoption on balanced data, or where latency and model size dominate, yields overhead without benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting
item.description: TensorLOB replaces the standard flattening of limit order book state into matrices with end-to-end tensor operations: mode-wise contractions for feature extraction and direct contraction with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, preserving the time, side, level, and attribute structure. The cost is a specialized tensor implementation, training effort on a domain-specific pipeline, and no quantified efficiency gain; compute savings are not claimed. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on the small FI-2010 benchmark, so gains may not transfer to other instruments, exchanges, or live data with nonstationarity and latency constraints. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: One Image Is Enough: Self-Generated Supervision for Personalizing Human Video Diffusion at Test Time
item.description: Replaces personalization via multi-pose subject videos or real multi-frame capture with self-generated supervision: a pose-conditioned generator synthesizes pseudo-ground-truth frames, an inference-time sampler filters them for identity consistency, and a per-subject low-rank adapter trains on static clips of the survivors. Costs include extra test-time compute per subject (candidate generation, identity scoring, and a small LoRA training run) plus pipeline complexity, and synthetic frames are explicitly lower in fidelity than real ones. Failure modes include the pseudo-GT generator or identity filter propagating reference-image errors into the adapter, degraded results when the target pose departs far from anything the generator synthesizes well, and per-subject adaptation latency that may not fit interactive serving budgets. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SHq: Learnable Grids for LLM Weight Quantization
item.description: SHq replaces the fixed lookup-table grids (INT, FP, NF, BOF) in block-scaled LUT quantization formats such as NF4, BOF4, and NVFP4 with a closed-form grid parameterized by a companding strength and an offset, requiring only modification of table contents. It costs a per-format grid selection or fitting step and reuses the otherwise-unused sign bit of the FP8 block scale; it adds no runtime latency or memory overhead since it is a drop-in grid replacement. It can fail if downstream kernels or hardware LUT instructions hardcode specific grids, if the optimal parameters do not transfer across models or layers, or if gains measured in KL divergence do not hold for the reader's specific tasks at very low bit-widths. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Introducing Cluster Efficiency to LLM Serving: Pooling Economical Accelerators over Fast Interconnects
item.description: The method replaces an eight-GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell server for long-context LLM serving with a Tenstorrent Galaxy cluster of pooled economical accelerators connected by fast interconnects. It requires specialized hardware with integrated communication engines, pipelined ring transfers, communication-computation overlap, and device-side decode replay, which imposes a high engineering and acquisition cost. The approach can fail if the interconnect is not sufficiently fast, as TCP-class communication reduces throughput by 23.5-67.4% and eliminates the cost advantage. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding
item.description: Replaces purely semantic SID construction and likelihood-only beam scoring in generative recommendation with utility-enriched semantic codes and beam scores augmented by predicted post-exposure utility. Costs include maintaining per-item utility estimates with incremental updates and training multiple post-exposure outcome predictors, though SID length, vocabulary, and decoding cost are unchanged. Can fail if utility predictors are inaccurate or drift faster than incremental code updates, causing beam scoring to mis-rank candidates, and the reported gain presupposes an existing deployed generative recommendation pipeline at platform scale. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis
item.description: The technique replaces per-topology sparse refactorization of the Jacobian with a single reference matrix inversion and low-rank Woodbury corrections for topology changes. It requires implementing a Newton--Raphson solver with inner iterative methods (truncated Neumann or BiCGStab) and storing the inverted reference matrix plus correction factors. The approach can fail if the spectral radius of the iteration matrix exceeds unity or if the condition number makes the reference Jacobian an ineffective preconditioner for specific outage scenarios. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Comparative study of global pooling for pre-departure ship fuel consumption prediction: Advantages over per-ship and adaptation-based approaches
item.description: Replaces per-vessel models and transfer or federated adaptation pipelines with a single LightGBM model trained on pooled fleet data, where each vessel is described by its identity and seven static specifications, using only inputs available before departure. Costs are modest: one model to train and maintain instead of many, no distributed infrastructure, and accuracy that does not improve further with per-vessel fine-tuning. It can fail for vessels whose specifications differ substantially from the training fleet, and its zero-shot advantage depends on specification coverage rather than on ship identity alone. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
